chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
That the inheritance of the child of al-mula'ana is for his mother; and if his mother is not alive, then for the closest people to his mother, his maternal uncles.
ai.seo_question: Who inherits from a child of al-mula'ana if the mother is deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the inheritance distribution for the child of *al-mula'ana*, a specific legal procedure where a husband and wife accuse each other of adultery without witnesses. It establishes that the mother is the primary heir, and upon her death, the estate passes to her maternal uncles (*al-akhwal*), reflecting the Shia juristic view of their closeness in lineage. This ruling highlights the distinct Shia perspective on kinship ties in inheritance cases where the paternal line is often excluded due to the uncertainty of paternity in *mula'ana*.
